card_says: Independent power producer created in 2008 to build and run the plant; the project's implementing agency and borrower under the guaranteed loans.
source_says: MIGA's project record states that KPDC "is now owned 56 percent by Globeleq and 44 percent by the government of Cameroon", Globeleq having acquired the shares previously held by AES; the guarantee for that investment was issued on 12 June 2014. The card's wording carries no owner and does not reflect the change of majority owner recorded by 2014.

source.title: Kribi Power Development Corporation

checked: Verified against the cited page: the 56/44 split, the acquisition of AES's shares and the 12 June 2014 guarantee date are all on it. Entry stands, already phrased with a date.

source.title: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report, FY 2024-25
source.publisher: KEC International Limited (filed with National Stock Exchange of India)

source_says: The company's own About page spells the name Wärtsilä and states that "Wärtsilä is listed on Nasdaq Helsinki". The card drops the diaereses.

card_says: Named as "Siemens France", preferred bidder with KEC India for the transmission line and substation contract.
source_says: Siemens' French press material names Siemens France Holding as the subsidiary of Siemens AG in France, and reports the revenue, staff and sites under the name Siemens France; the article's lead-in names the local entity Siemens SAS France. The three names appear in different places in the same document.
checked: Corrected. The writer concluded that "'Siemens France' is a descriptive label rather than a registered company name". The page does not support that: it is the page's own reporting entity for revenue and headcount. Siemens SAS France appears only in the lead-in, not in the boilerplate as the writer had it. The entry is reduced to which name appears where.

company: Ministère de l'Équipement et des Transports, Mali
card_says: The ministry that published the compensation and resettlement framework for the Malian sections of the corridor and held the Bamako to Bougouni and Sikasso to Heremakono works.
source_says: A ministry of that title existed when Décret n°02-498/P-RM of 5 November 2002 set out ministers' duties, its attributions being set at article 9. Décret n°2012-486/P-RM of 4 September 2012 contains no ministry of this title: article 14 gives "Ministre de l'Equipement et de l'Aménagement du Territoire" and article 15 "Ministre des Transports et des Infrastructures Routières". For the later years of the corridor works no ministry carried this title.

source.title: Décret n°02-498/P-RM du 5 novembre 2002 and Décret n°2012-486/P-RM du 4 septembre 2012 fixant les attributions spécifiques des membres du Gouvernement, Journal Officiel

checked: Verified against both Journal Officiel PDFs. Entry stands, with the exact successor titles and the article numbers added; the 2002 decree is now cited alongside the 2012 one, since the entry rests on both.

card_says: The national roads directorate of Argentina, inside the public works ministry.
source_says: The agency's own FAQ page describes Vialidad Nacional as a decentralised body "actuante en la órbita de la Secretaría de Transporte" within the Ministerio de Economía; Resolución 1136/2025 describes it as a decentralised body "bajo la órbita del MINISTERIO DE ECONOMIA" and names no secretariat. The same resolution cites Decreto 461/2025 of 7 July 2025, which began a reorganisation of decentralised agencies including Vialidad, article 36 providing that their top authorities "continuarán ejerciendo transitoriamente sus funciones y atribuciones" until new structures are approved. Neither page says which ministry it sat under at the time of the case.

source.title: Preguntas frecuentes - Vialidad; Resolución 1136/2025
source.publisher: Gobierno de Argentina; Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina

checked: Corrected. The writer's entry ended "It sat under the public works ministry at the time of the case", which neither cited page states - it restates the card and reads as a confirmation of it. Removed, and replaced with the unreconciled difference between the two pages on whether a secretariat sits between the agency and the ministry. Decree number and article added.

card_says: The state joint-stock company that took full ownership and management of the Balakhani landfill on 14 October 2009.
source_says: The company's own site adds that a presidential order of 22 September 2021 placed Tamiz Shahar under the management of Azerbaijan Investment Holding, and that collection and transport of all solid household waste in Baku remain under the authority of the Baku City Executive Power rather than the company, which is responsible for placement and neutralisation.
checked: Verified against the cited page, including the 22 September 2021 order. Entry stands, already dated. The card's own 14 October 2009 date is not contradicted by the page, which gives 6 August 2008 for the creating decree and 12 March 2009 for the start of work - three different dates for three different events, not a conflict.
